political_impact.text: The Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes were paid the appraised value of the land, $28,955.48, about $1.56 an acre.
Congress let the President enlarge the range to as much as 20,000 acres with the leftover 1908 money; 18,523.85 acres were reserved by a schedule approved June 10, 1909.
political_impact.source: Act of March 4, 1909, ch. 301, 35 Stat. 1051; 437 F.2d 458, Finding 15

political_impact.text: The American Bison Society closed its herd fund at $10,560.50 and bought thirty-four bison from the Conrad estate herd at Kalispell at $275 a head delivered.
political_impact.source: American Bison Society, Third Annual Report (1910), pp. 4–5

political_impact.text: Thirty-seven bison went onto the fenced range on October 17, 1909.

legacy.text: The herd became one of the anchor herds that pulled the plains bison back from the edge; the white bison Big Medicine lived on the range from 1933 to 1959.

The Court of Claims held that the bison-range land had been taken under eminent domain within the meaning of the Fifth Amendment, as part of a $6,066,668.78 judgment covering all lands disposed of under the 1904 allotment act.
legacy.source: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes v. United States, 437 F.2d 458 (Ct. Cl. 1971)

legacy.text: Congress placed all land of the National Bison Range in trust for the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes and repealed the 1908 provision.
legacy.source: Montana Water Rights Protection Act, Pub. L. 116-260, Div. DD, §12; 86 Fed. Reg. 33345

legacy.text: The Tribes took over full day-to-day management of the range.

today.name: CSKT Bison Range
today.note: Held in trust for and managed by the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes; formerly the National Bison Range in the National Wildlife Refuge System.
